title: Dental Calculus Field-Sampling Protocol
author: Christina Warinner
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7hphj5n
materials: Wrap your tube rack in foil.
Replace top layer of your gloves.

steps.title: Wear double gloves
steps.instruction: Put on two pairs of gloves; replace the outer pair after each sampling.

steps.title: Prepare metadata and tube labels
steps.instruction: Fill in the metadata sheet with the corresponding tube IDs and write the sample name or label on a piece of paper.

steps.title: Construct foil bowl
steps.instruction: Make a foil bowl that is wide enough to fit the tooth, your hands and the dental scalar, has a smooth internal surface, and will let calculus fall directly into the tube.

steps.title: Position bowl on rack
steps.instruction: Place the foil bowl on the tube rack and press the tube through the bottom of the bowl and the foil of the rack so the fit is snug.

steps.title: Inspect tooth and calculus
steps.instruction: Grasp the tooth root, locate the dental calculus, gently brush away surface dirt with a dental scalar away from the bowl or tube, avoid touching the calculus with anything other than the scalar, and check for fractures or weakened integrity; if any are found, consult the collection curator before proceeding.

steps.title: Photograph whole tooth
steps.instruction: Place the tooth on or next to the labelled paper, include a scale if possible, and take photographs of the whole tooth and close‑up views of the calculus from several angles, ensuring the sample label is clearly visible.

steps.title: Hold tooth for sampling
steps.instruction: Hold the tooth by the root with the crown oriented so the calculus will fall directly down into the bowl; position the tooth in the centre of the bowl, slightly below the rim.

steps.title: Sterilize utensils before use
steps.instruction: Wipe all utensils with alcohol wipes or paper towels dampened with bleach; if bleach is used, rinse metal utensils with preferably HPLC‑grade water to remove residual bleach and prevent corrosion.

steps.title: Detach calculus with scalar
steps.instruction: Using a sterile dental scalar, apply downward pressure with the broad flat edge to break off the calculus deposit so it falls into the tube; if resistance is encountered, scrape gently along the tooth surface toward the bowl, increasing pressure as needed; if the deposit becomes powdery, scrape directly into the tube; always use a scalar (not a dental pick) and avoid damaging the occlusal surface.

steps.title: Record calculus location
steps.instruction: Enter the location of the selected calculus deposit (e.g., lingual, buccal) and any disease or consolidant information on the metadata sheet.

steps.title: Retrieve calculus if needed
steps.instruction: If the calculus has not fallen into the bowl, use sterile forceps or tweezers to move the deposit directly into the tube.

steps.title: Seal and store tube
steps.instruction: Close the cap of the tube, place the tube in a pre‑labelled sample bag, and discard the foil bowl apparatus.

steps.title: Photograph sampling site
steps.instruction: Photograph the tooth again, focusing on the sampling site and ensuring the sample ID is visible; then return the tooth to its sample bag.

steps.title: Sterilize utensils after use
steps.instruction: Wipe all used utensils with an alcohol wipe or bleach‑dampened paper towel; if bleach was used, rinse metal utensils with preferably HPLC water afterwards.

steps.title: Record additional observations
steps.instruction: Note any other observations from sampling, such as an approximate weight of the calculus sample.

steps.title: Replace gloves and repeat
steps.instruction: Replace gloves and repeat the sampling preparation for the next tooth (return to step 1).

steps.title: Label bags and tubes
steps.instruction: Label all bags for placing the corresponding tubes in, and label each tube ready for sampling.
